cases.exposure_context_quote: approximately 40 min after intentional self-ingestion of AlP tablets that were fully dissolved in clean water during an acute emotional distress episode in early 2026
cases.agent: aluminum phosphide (15 tablets, 3 g each, 56% purity; total 25.2 g)
cases.agent_quote: He ingested a total of 15 AlP tablets, each weighing 3 g with a purity of 56%, resulting in a total ingested dose of 25.2 g, equivalent to 16–25 times the reported human lethal dose (1.0–1.5 g).
cases.circumstance: intentional self-ingestion during an acute emotional distress episode; attempts at self-induced vomiting unsuccessful

symptoms.quote: the patient rapidly developed progressive dizziness, oppressive chest tightness, shortness of breath, and an unsteady gait

he appeared markedly anxious and hemodynamically unstable. Vital signs were as follows: blood pressure, 95/70 mmHg; heart rate, 112 beats/min; respiratory rate, 26 breaths/min; and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), 94% while breathing room air.

symptoms.finding: ECG: diffuse ST-segment depression and symmetric T-wave inversion (myocardial ischemia)
symptoms.quote: A 12-lead electrocardiogram demonstrated diffuse ST-segment depression and symmetric T-wave inversion across the precordial and lateral leads, consistent with severe phosphine-induced myocardial ischemia and subendocardial injury

symptoms.finding: acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and progressive somnolence
symptoms.quote: the patient's clinical status deteriorated acutely, with the development of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and progressive somnolence

symptoms.finding: ARDS (bilateral ground-glass opacities on CT day 3)
symptoms.quote: Chest computed tomography (CT) performed on day 3 revealed bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities (Figure 2(a)), consistent with acute lung injury and ARDS secondary to phosphine toxicity.
a subsequent sputum culture identified C. koseri, confirming the diagnosis of VAP.

labs.name: arterial blood gas pH
labs.quote: Arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe metabolic acidosis with pH = 7.223, bicarbonate (HCO₃−) = 14.4 mmol/L, and a critically elevated blood lactate level of 13.15 mmol/L

labs.name: bicarbonate
labs.quote: Arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe metabolic acidosis with pH = 7.223, bicarbonate (HCO₃−) = 14.4 mmol/L, and a critically elevated blood lactate level of 13.15 mmol/L

labs.name: blood lactate
labs.quote: the blood lactate level further increased to 14.75 mmol/L

labs.name: Glasgow Coma Scale
labs.quote: the patient was fully alert with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15

labs.name: serum aluminum
labs.quote: His serum aluminum level was detectable biochemically, confirming the systemic absorption of AlP.

labs.name: hypocalcemia
labs.quote: A definitive diagnosis of MODS was established, characterized by acute kidney injury, overt myocardial damage, refractory lactic acidosis, and hypocalcemia.

treatment.name: ultra-early gastric lavage with 200 mL liquid paraffin
treatment.quote: ultra-early gastric decontamination was performed immediately using 200 mL of liquid paraffin to coat residual AlP tablets and halt further phosphine gas production

treatment.name: activated charcoal and mannitol catharsis
treatment.quote: followed by activated charcoal adsorption and mannitol-induced catharsis to minimize ongoing toxin absorption

treatment.name: hemoperfusion (two sessions)
treatment.quote: The first session of hemoperfusion was promptly initiated to actively eliminate circulating lipophilic phosphine and aluminum ions.

treatment.name: continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH)
treatment.quote: Continuous venovenous hemofiltration was promptly initiated for sustained organ support, metabolic stabilization, and cytokine clearance.

treatment.name: endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation with prone positioning
treatment.quote: Emergency endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation were initiated to secure the airway and support gas exchange.

treatment.name: norepinephrine, dopamine, metaraminol vasopressors
treatment.quote: Vasopressor support during the first 72 h consisted of dopamine (total 800 mg), metaraminol (40 mg), and norepinephrine (6 mg)

treatment.name: 5% sodium bicarbonate infusion (1500 mL over first 24 h)
treatment.quote: 1500 mL of 5% sodium bicarbonate (equivalent to approximately 893 mEq bicarbonate) was continuously infused intravenously over the initial 24-hour resuscitation period.

treatment.name: high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone
treatment.quote: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone and prone positioning ventilation were administered to reduce pulmonary inflammation and improve oxygenation.

treatment.name: targeted antimicrobial therapy for C. koseri VAP
treatment.quote: Antimicrobial therapy was promptly adjusted according to the microbiological culture and antimicrobial susceptibility results.

treatment.name: vitamin C and cytochrome C antioxidant therapy
treatment.quote: vitamin C (total dose of 30.5 g, 2 g per day) and cytochrome C (total dose of 1260 mg, 60 mg per day) for 21 days

treatment.name: fluid resuscitation (3500 mL crystalloids first 24 h; ~33.8 L total)
treatment.quote: aggressive fluid resuscitation with a total of 3500 mL of crystalloids (normal saline and Ringer's lactate) over the first 24 h

cases.icu_admission: yes (mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, CVVH in ICU setting)
cases.outcome: full clinical recovery, discharged day 18 post-admission
cases.outcome_quote: The patient achieved full clinical recovery and was discharged from the hospital on day 18 post-admission, with near-normalization of all biochemical markers (Table 1).
cases.notes: MODS with refractory cardiogenic shock, ARDS, AKI, liver dysfunction, hypocalcemia, and secondary C. koseri VAP; treated without ECMO. Extubated hospital day 4; repeat ECG day 5 normalized.
